page: Microsoft Azure E4-2s_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine engineered for workloads requiring high memory capacity alongside restricted CPU core counts. Operating on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization, the instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at a base frequency of 2.8 GHz. The hardware configuration allocates 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads. It features a memory capacity of 32.0 GB, yielding a high ratio of 16.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance does not include bundled local storage or GPU accelerators, requiring attached remote storage for file systems and data persistence.

Benchmark evaluations reflect the architectural constraints of running on a single physical core. Single-threaded performance achieves average baseline levels, marked by a Geekbench single-core score of 1313.0, a stress-ng single-core score of 1418.79, and gzip compression throughput of 23.94 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-threaded metrics rank in the bottom decile due to limited thread concurrency, with Geekbench multi-core scoring 1538.0 and PassMark CPU reaching 2239.89. Memory performance benchmarks indicate 85.83 GB/sec on cached read operations and 10.67 GB/sec on uncached large-block reads, with Redis throughput reaching 1.64 million SET operations per second.

The primary operational advantage of the E4-2s_v4 lies in licensing efficiency. By constraining a 4-vCPU hardware footprint down to 2 active vCPUs while preserving the complete 32.0 GB memory allocation, it reduces commercial software licensing costs that scale on a per-core basis. The primary tradeoff is the strict bottleneck on CPU-bound and highly concurrent tasks. The instance fits database engines with modest query concurrency, memory-intensive middleware, in-memory caching nodes, and enterprise software stacks bound by per-core licensing models.
description: Microsoft Azure E4-2s_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine operating on Microsoft Hyper-V and powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8370C processor at 2.8 GHz. It delivers 2 dedicated vCPUs across 1 physical core and hyper-threading, accompanied by 32.0 GB of system memory. The server provisions no local disk storage and no GPU acceleration, necessitating external storage volumes. Benchmark data demonstrates standard single-core execution capacity, while parallel processing and memory bandwidth are limited by the two-thread total, yielding lower multi-core and database operational throughput. This constrained-core configuration offers qualitative cost efficiency for database and enterprise software systems licensed on a per-vCPU basis that require substantial memory per thread. The instance is suitable for small relational database deployments, in-memory key-value caching layers, and memory-heavy backend services with moderate CPU concurrency demands.
